items.titleZh: 斯特拉：「非常令人沮丧的周六」，巴库暴露迈凯伦直道速度短板
items.summaryZh: 迈凯伦继中国站、加拿大站之后，本季第三次颗粒无收。领队安德烈亚·斯特拉说，这是「非常令人沮丧的周六」，有问题也有失误，但更暴露了赛车在这类赛道上的根本局限：弯道不够快，「更主要的是直道不够快」，车手整场都在被攻击，「几乎都在看后视镜，而不是想怎么往前追」。
items.originalTitle: 'A very frustrating Saturday' – Andrea Stella explains how Baku highlighted McLaren’s straight line weakness
detailZh: 迈凯伦领队安德烈亚·斯特拉解释了迈凯伦在阿塞拜疆大奖赛上表现受限的原因。
继中国站和加拿大站之后，迈凯伦今年第三次一分未得，在阿塞拜疆度过了一个痛苦的下午。
最令人沮丧的是，奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里本来迎来了他在坎坷的2026赛季迄今最好的表现，在比赛大部分时间里跑在第二，看起来即将登上领奖台。
然而，他在比赛最后几圈的一次失误让他冲进了1号弯的缓冲区。由于安全车让车阵挤在一起，他还没来得及重新回到赛道，就跌出了前十。
与此同时，兰多·诺里斯度过了一个混乱的周末，他受到动力单元问题的困扰，在直道上比队友损失了一点性能。
他本来至少能拿到一些安慰性的积分，直到在弗朗哥·科拉平托与皮埃尔·加斯利的碰撞中遭到殃及。这位世界冠军不仅被撞出了比赛，还损失了一些在巴库引入的升级部件。
「这是一个非常令人沮丧的周六，」领队安德烈亚·斯特拉说，「我觉得我们遇到了问题，也有一些失误，但与此同时，我认为我们为赛车套件在这类赛道上的一些根本局限付出了代价，因为我们在弯道里不够快。
「但与此同时，更主要的是我们在直道上不够快，这让我们的车手不断暴露在被攻击的境地，整场比赛几乎都在看后视镜，而不是思考怎样在比赛中向前推进。」
斯特拉强调，皮亚斯特里在这种情况下表现出色，更关键的是，他似乎已经克服了一直困扰他驾驭2026年赛车的问题。
「奥斯卡这种防守型的比赛跑得非常好，」斯特拉说，「他非常精准。他的比赛让我想起了他在2024年赢下这场比赛时的表现，当时他长时间把（夏尔·）勒克莱尔挡在身后。
「但不幸的是，进站换上表现不如软胎的中性胎之后，他出现了锁死，比赛就此结束。
「这对奥斯卡来说真的很可惜，因为他应该有机会去争夺领奖台，也因为奥斯卡整个周末都开得非常好。我们知道奥斯卡正处在适应2026年赛车的学习曲线中，能得到回报本来会很好。」
斯特拉承认，影响诺里斯排位赛的动力单元问题并没有消失，让他的日子更加难过。
「如果我们看兰多的比赛，以及他逐渐往后掉的事实，这有几个原因，」他说，「比赛中我们偶尔也看到了同样的问题，但没有排位赛时那么系统性。
「它有点间歇性，但在喷油这个问题上肯定存在很大的改进空间，比赛中我们在奥斯卡的赛车上也偶尔看到了这一点。所以这是我们需要高度优先处理的问题。
「除此之外，兰多被速度更快的（马克斯·）维斯塔潘超越了。兰多在中性胎上有点挣扎——我提到维斯塔潘，是因为他和兰多一样用的是中性胎，但他更快。不过要称赞奥斯卡，奥斯卡成功把维斯塔潘挡在了身后。
「在兰多这边，我们在动力单元能量释放上有点吃力，而且兰多的驾驶也有一些不稳定。在被（刘易斯·）汉密尔顿超越时，他出现了锁死，还有几次失误，让后面的车进入了攻击范围。而一旦对手进入攻击范围，我们就很难防守，这又回到了极速的问题上。」
斯特拉承认这对诺里斯来说是一个棘手的周末：「我想说，对兰多而言，这总体上是他在2026年经历过的最困难的比赛之一，我们需要从中吸取教训，看看有什么可以改进。
「但我想说，大部分改进空间在车队和赛车这边，因为我们需要为车手提供一台更适合比赛、在可预测性上更稳定的赛车。」
极速问题一向很复杂，从来不只是纯粹的马力问题。
「我认为作为一支车队，我们需要研究为什么赛车在这些长直道上没有达到应有的竞争力，」斯特拉说，「而且很明显，这不是单一因素造成的。当然，我们一直相当公开透明地表示，我们需要改善赛车的空气阻力。
「还有几个因素，比如涉及我们的齿比——我们需要检查自己是否选对了齿比，才能在这种讲究极速的赛道上竞争。
「与此同时，当我们查看数据并与（梅赛德斯）比较时，我们发现我们的动力单元没有优化到位。我认为，排位赛时我们几乎把动力单元能提供的都发挥出来了，但有几个项目我们没能优化，于是在正赛中付出了代价。所以在动力单元方面还有一些工作要做。」
巴库的升级套件以慢弯性能为目标，尽管车队周末令人失望，这套升级仍带来了令人鼓舞的结果。
「我们很满意，」斯特拉说，「数据似乎证实升级没有问题，所以希望在接下来的比赛中能带来更多收益。这是整个车队付出的巨大努力。」
他承认一些部件可能在撞车中损失了，但相信替换件会及时到位。
「不幸的是，我想有几个部件在撞车中损失了，这也是卷入这类情况的另一个坏处。但幸运的是，还有一些新部件正在运来，所以接下来的比赛我们应该没问题。」
斯特拉还确认，迈凯伦的研发重心已经转向明年的赛车，只有此前已批准的更新仍会用到MCL40上。
「还会有一批零件陆续送到赛道，所以我们仍会看到一些新零件用在MCL40上。但就目前而言，所有的精力都已经集中在明年的赛车上，我们在赛道上看到的新东西，是几周前放行的零件的结果。」
（来源：Formula 1 官网）
detailEn: McLaren Team Principal Andrea Stella has explained why McLaren's performance was limited in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
For the third time this year after China and Canada, McLaren failed to score a point in Azerbaijan as they endured a painful afternoon.

The huge frustration was that Oscar Piastri had enjoyed his best showing thus far of a troubled 2026 season, and the Australian looked set to log a podium finish, having run second for much of the race.
However, a mistake in the closing laps saw him head down the Turn 1 escape road, and given that the field had been bunched up by the Safety Car, he tumbled out of the top 10 before he could resume.
Lando Norris meanwhile had a messy weekend, suffering with a PU issue that cost him a little performance on the straights relative to his team mate.

He was at least destined to pick up some consolation points before he became collateral damage after the Franco Colapinto/Pierre Gasly collision. Not only was the World Champion bundled out of the race, he also lost some of the upgraded parts that had been introduced in Baku.

“It's been a very frustrating Saturday,” said Team Principal Andrea Stella. “I think we had issues and some mistakes, but at the same time I think we paid some fundamental limitations of our package in this kind of circuit, because we were not fast enough in the corners.

“But at the same time, mainly we were not fast enough in the straights, and this continuously exposed our drivers to being attacked and having to spend their race pretty much watching the mirrors rather than thinking at how they can progress in the race.”
Stella stressed that Piastri had done a great job in the circumstances, and crucially he appeared to have got on top of the issues that have been hampering him with the 2026 car.

“Oscar did this sort of defensive race very well,” said Stella. “He was very precise. His race reminded me very much of what he did in 2024 to win the race, when he held [Charles] Leclerc behind for a long time.
“But unfortunately, after the pit stop and having gone on the medium tyres, which were performing worse than the soft tyres, he had a lock-up and his race finished there.

“It's a real shame for Oscar, because he deserved to have a go at fighting for the podium, and also because Oscar has been driving very well the entire weekend. And we know that Oscar was in a little bit of learning trajectory to adapt to the 2026 car, and it would have been good to be rewarded.”
Stella admitted that life was made even harder for Norris by the PU issue that had hindered him in Qualifying, and which didn’t go away.

“If we look at Lando's race and the fact that he gradually went backwards, there's a few reasons for that,” he said. “We occasionally saw the same problem during the race, but not as systematic as in Qualifying.

"It was a little bit intermittent, but definitely there's a significant opportunity on the topic of fuel injection that we saw occasionally also on Oscar's car during the race. So this is a topic that we should look at high priority.

“In addition to that, Lando was overtaken by [Max] Verstappen, that was a quicker car. Lando was struggling a bit with the medium tyres – I mentioned Verstappen because he was on medium tyres as well as Lando, but he was faster. But credit to Oscar, Oscar managed to keep Verstappen behind.

“On Lando's side, we were struggling a little bit with power unit deployment, and also Lando was having some inconsistencies in his driving. When he was overtaken by [Lewis] Hamilton, he had a lock-up, and he had a few mistakes that meant that cars behind were within range. And when they are within range, then we struggle to defend, which goes back to the point on top speed.”

Stella conceded that it was a tricky weekend for Norris: “I would say that for Lando, this was one of the most difficult events in general that he has experienced in 2026, something that we need to take away, looking at whatever can be improved.

“But I would say most of the opportunities lie on the team side, and on the car side, because we need to be able to offer our drivers a car that is more raceable and just more consistent in terms of predictability.”
The top speed equation is always a complicated one, and it’s never just about pure horsepower.

“We need to look, I think, as a team, as to why the car wasn't as competitive as it should be in these long straights,” said Stella. “And it is very apparent that it is not a single factor. Certainly, we have always talked quite openly and transparently that we need to improve the aerodynamic drag of the car.
“There are a few factors, which refer to our ratios for instance – we need to look whether we are on the right ratios to compete in circuits in which you have this sort of top speed.

“And at the same time, when we look at the data and we compare with [Mercedes], we see that our power unit was not optimised. I think, while for Qualifying we managed to exploit pretty much the most that was available in the power unit, there's a few items that we were not able to optimise, and we paid the price in the race. So there's some work to do on the power unit side.”
The Baku upgrade package, which targeted slow-corner performance, delivered encouraging results despite the team's disappointing weekend.

“We are happy," said Stella. "The data seems to confirm that there's no issues with the upgrades, so hopefully there will be more benefit at the coming races. This has been a great effort by the entire team."
He admitted some components may have been lost in the crash but was confident replacements would arrive in time.

“Unfortunately, I think a couple of parts will have been lost with the crash, which is another downside of having been involved in these sorts of situations. But luckily, there's some more new parts coming, so we should be okay for the coming races.”
Stella also confirmed McLaren's development focus has switched to next year's car, with only previously approved updates still due to reach the MCL40.

“There's a tail of parts that will land trackside, so we will see still some new parts coming to the MCL40. But at the moment, as we speak, all the efforts are already concentrated onto next year's car, and what we see coming trackside is the result of parts being released a few weeks ago.”

Source: Formula 1 (formula1.com). Original article: https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/a-very-frustrating-saturday-stella-explains-how-baku-highlighted-mclarens-straight-line-weakness.4iY4EWmrhkVVgus2tothvn

items.originalTitle: Alpine makes statement as Franco Colapinto-related abuse accelerates
items.summaryEn: Alpine's Formula 1 team has once again spoken out against social media abuse after a surge of hateful comments following Franco Colapinto's crash at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
detailZh: 在弗朗哥·科拉平托相关网络暴力加速升级之际，阿尔派发表声明
在阿塞拜疆大奖赛期间社交媒体上出现更多网络暴力后，阿尔派正在采取立场
弗朗科·科拉平托、阿尔派、兰多·诺里斯、迈凯伦
在弗朗科·科拉平托于阿塞拜疆大奖赛中发生撞车之后，阿尔派一级方程式车队再次公开发声，反对社交媒体上的网络暴力。
最近，阿根廷车迷的行为因一波波恶意评论而受到审视。这些评论矛头指向国际汽联的赛事干事以及阿尔派车队，原因是科拉平托在赞德沃特因双黄旗下超车被处以一次通过维修区处罚。
皮埃尔·加斯利也成了辱骂的目标，此前这位法国车手在马德里一度拒绝让他的阿尔平队友通过。加斯利透露，威胁甚至波及他的家人；科拉平托则温和地表示这种行为“看着不舒服”，同时坚称“不仅仅是他的车迷”所为。
本周末在巴库，科拉平托失去控制，在安全车重启时引发连环撞车，导致加斯利和兰多·诺里斯双双退赛。卫冕冠军尤其恼火，在还没来得及亲自查看画面之前，他就表示无论谁造成这次撞车都应该“至少被禁赛一场”。
虽然诺里斯甚至没有点名提到科拉平托，但这还是在社交媒体上再次引发了辱骂——主要针对这位英国车手，但加斯利和其他人也未能幸免。
“在极限状态下 racing 时失误难免会发生，无论结果如何，任何人都不应该遭受充满仇恨或辱骂性的评论，”阿尔派 车队在周日的一份声明中坚称。
车队特意避免激怒自己车手的粉丝群体：“谴责社交媒体上的辱骂行为并非针对任何一个粉丝群体，也不是针对某支车队或某位车手的支持者，这是普遍性的问题，应该向这项运动的所有车迷指出并得到正视。
“正如我们在以往类似事件中所说，我们强烈谴责部分车迷在网络上的反应，并与一级方程式、国际汽联以及其他车队站在一起，决心根除这种现象。在最近的几场比赛中，这种情况已经屡见不鲜，绝不能被纵容。”
这起最新的辱骂事件发生前不久，据报道 阿尔派 一级方程式车队老板弗拉维奥·布里亚托利曾威胁阿根廷媒体，如果仇恨言论继续蔓延、损害车队的声誉，就不让他们再采访科拉平托。
“作为一支车队，我们认为有必要再次就阿塞拜疆大奖赛之后网络上的仇恨和辱骂言论发声。这些言论不仅针对我们的一位车手，还针对一级方程式大家庭的其他成员，包括媒体，以及我们在赛车运动巅峰领域所尊重、敬仰并乐于与之竞争的车队同行。在极限状态下比赛难免会出现失误，无论结果或结局如何，任何人都不应该遭受仇恨或辱骂性的评论。”
“谴责社交媒体上的辱骂行为并非针对任何一个车迷群体或某支车队、某位车手的支持者，这是普遍性的问题，应该向这项运动的所有车迷指出并加以重视。正如我们此前多次所说，我们强烈谴责部分车迷在网上的过激反应，并与一级方程式、国际汽联以及其他车队站在一起，希望彻底杜绝这种现象。这在近几场比赛中已成为常态，绝不能被容忍。”
“我们知道，作为这项运动中一名自豪的参与者和利益相关方，我们有责任发出声音，并帮助推动寻找解决方案。我们将继续与锦标赛推广方和版权方，以及管理机构密切合作，探讨应对网络辱骂的方法，倡导健康的体育竞争——这正是一级方程式享誉世界、如此特别的原因。”
detailEn: Alpine makes statement as Franco Colapinto-related abuse accelerates
Following further abuse on social media amid the Azerbaijan GP, Alpine is taking a stand
Franco Colapinto, Alpine, Lando Norris, McLaren
The Alpine Formula 1 team has again spoken out against social media abuse following Franco Colapinto’s shunt in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Argentinian fans’ behaviour has been scrutinised lately following waves of hateful comments. Those were aimed at FIA stewards and the Alpine squad when Colapinto was handed a drive-through penalty for overtaking under a double yellow flag in Zandvoort.

Pierre Gasly was at the receiving end of abuse too after the Frenchman briefly refused to let his Alpine team-mate through in Madrid. Gasly revealed the threats targeted his family too; Colapinto meekly labelled the behaviour as “not nice to see” while insisting it was ‘not just his fans’.

This weekend in Baku, Colapinto lost control and caused a pile-up at a safety car restart, taking both Gasly and Lando Norris out of the race. The reigning champion was particularly upset and, before being able to view the footage himself, suggested whoever caused the crash should get “at least a one-race ban”.
While Norris did not even refer to Colapinto by name, this did trigger abuse on social media yet again – mainly aimed at the Briton, but Gasly and others weren’t spared.
“Mistakes happen when racing at the limit and no matter the result or outcome, nobody should be subject to hateful or abusive comments,” Alpine insisted in a statement on Sunday.

The team made a point of not antagonising its own driver’s fanbase: “Condemning abuse on social media is not aimed at any one fan base or the supporters of one team or driver, this is universal and should be called out and recognised to all fans of the sport.

“As we have said in previous instances, we strongly condemn the reaction of some fans online and stand in solidarity with Formula One, the FIA, and other teams in wanting to stamp it out. It has become a regular occurrence in recent races and cannot be condoned.”

The latest abuse has occurred shortly after Alpine F1 boss Flavio Briatore reportedly threatened Argentinian media not to let them speak to Colapinto again if the hatred kept being spewed, damaging the outfit’s reputation.

“As a team, we feel it’s necessary to speak out once more about the hate and abuse online following the Azerbaijan Grand Prix. Not only aimed at one of our own drivers, but also members of the Formula One community, including media, and to our racing counterparts who we respect, admire, and revel competing against in the pinnacle of motorsport. Mistakes happen when racing at the limit and no matter the result or outcome, nobody should be subject to hateful or abusive comments.

“Condemning abuse on social media is not aimed at any one fan base or the supporters of one team or driver, this is universal and should be called out and recognised to all fans of the sport. As we have said in previous instances, we strongly condemn the reaction of some fans online and stand in solidarity with Formula One, the FIA, and other teams in wanting to stamp it out. It has become a regular occurrence in recent races and cannot be condoned.

“We know as a proud participant and stakeholder in the sport, we hold a responsibility to speak out and also help support in finding a solution. We will continue to work closely with the championship promoter and rights-holder, and the governing body to discuss ways in which to tackle online abuse and encourage healthy sporting rivalry, which Formula One is renowned for and what makes it so special.”
keyPointsZh: 此前阿根廷车迷因科拉平托在双黄旗下超车被罚通过维修区，而将仇恨言论指向国际汽联干事和阿尔派车队。
keyPointsEn: Argentinian fans previously directed hateful comments at FIA stewards and the Alpine squad after Colapinto received a drive-through penalty for overtaking under a double yellow flag.

items.titleZh: 安东内利通过了皮亚斯特里曾未能通过的关键考验
items.summaryZh: 安东内利坦言阿塞拜疆大奖赛周末是他本赛季“迄今为止最糟”的比赛，但他展现了如何在糟糕的周末中限制损失，成功通过了争夺世界冠军途中不可避免的一次考验，避免了皮亚斯特里去年冲击F1总冠军时在巴库遭遇的崩盘命运。

media.altZh: 安东内利通过了皮亚斯特里曾未能通过的关键考验 · 第 1 张

items.originalTitle: Antonelli passed a key test Piastri had failed
items.summaryEn: Kimi Antonelli called his Azerbaijan Grand Prix weekend the worst of his season, yet he showed he knows how to limit the damage on a bad weekend, passing a test he would inevitably face and avoiding the fate that befell Oscar Piastri in Baku during his unsuccessful title pursuit.
detailZh: 世界冠军不只靠好日子赢下，糟糕的日子同样决定成败。
基米·安东内利的阿塞拜疆大奖赛周末——他自己正确地形容为“本赛季迄今最糟糕的周末”——正是这一点的证明，他通过了迟早都会面对的一次考验，而且表现出色。这样做，他避免了去年奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里在冲击一级方程式冠军失败途中遭遇的命运。
尽量减少这种糟糕表现是夺冠方程式的一部分，但更关键的是在出问题时控制损失。我们知道安东内利带着高达81分的巨大领先优势进入这个周末，而他在巴库展示的是他懂得如何使用这个优势。这正是皮亚斯特里没能做到的——他2025年带着31分的领先优势来到巴库，虽然不那么悬殊，但依然健康。
皮亚斯特里在排位赛中撞车，发车前抢跑，明知即使排名暴跌也难逃处罚，随后又在第一圈的5号弯撞车。唯一的慰藉是迈凯伦队友、冠军争夺对手兰多·诺里斯没有充分利用这个机会，但即便如此，这标志着皮亚斯特里的夺冠征程开始瓦解。
在那一年巴西大奖赛的比赛周末，我曾问及他的困境，他提到了阿塞拜疆站，说那个周末“可以说有一些其他因素可能悄悄混了进来”，影响了他的表现。很难不得出这样的结论：他指的是蒙扎“木瓜规则”事件的余波——当时因为队友诺里斯进站较慢，他被车队下令让诺里斯超越。
即使没有车队指令令人困惑这一复杂因素的干扰，安东内利也本可能轻易遭遇类似的局面，尤其是考虑到他经验尚浅，此前他在第一节排位赛中不必要地撞上了护墙。
这是一个重大失误，因为在排位赛这么早的阶段完全没必要冒险。这个失误或许是为了缩小与梅赛德斯队友乔治·拉塞尔之间速度差距而用力过猛的结果，或许也与他今年一贯倾向于过度贴近赛道边缘的老毛病有关，但尽管他本不该犯这个错误，他却以完全正确的心态投入了正赛。
他最终 Recovery 到第五名有安全车的帮助，但这是一场稳健、执行到位的比赛：他在与奥利·比尔曼的碰撞中无辜受损、车底板受伤之后，又在第一次安全车重启的1号弯混乱中保持冷静，刻意留出了余量，稳住了自己的头脑。
安东内利说：“我开得有点像我奶奶，完全就是避免受损的安全模式，完全不冒险。在做动作之前，我都会先确认自己有把握才去做。”
这展现出一种与他缺乏经验不相称的成熟——对于学习速度没那么快的车手来说，这种智慧往往要付出高昂代价、经历惨痛教训才能换来。他后来详细解释了自己这样做的理由，同时也表示，在大奖赛刚开始时，他很快就放下了想要复制蒙扎式翻盘的幻想。虽然他在排位赛后表示自己“已经没有什么可输的了”，但赛后接受采访时，他解释了为什么实际上并非如此。
安东内利说：“如果我有蒙扎那站或者之前几场比赛那样的节奏，结果就会不一样。那就会是全力进攻。但我很早就意识到，首先，当一长串车都处在尝试超车的状态下，超车会难得多。而且我的节奏也不如之前。所以心态很快就转变了。
而且看到那么多人犯错，你也会稍微收敛一点。我只是利用了其他所有人的失误，就这样向前赶了上去。
梅赛德斯车队领队托托·沃尔夫以及他身边的人肯定会反复向他灌输这种处理方式，但只有安东内利自己才能锁定一种与平时让他受益匪浅的进攻型心态相悖的思维模式。结果就是他在积分榜上落后拉塞尔15分而不是25分。这是一个沉重的打击，但还不算最糟的。
假如他当时过于激进，发生撞车或与对手碰撞退赛，那损失的不只是积分，还有他会带进赛季末冲刺阶段的心理创伤。相反，安东内利以自己形容为八成力度的表现完成了这场比赛，对自己的处理方式感到满意，并能在接下来的马来西亚大奖赛上向拉塞尔发出挑战。
他说：“下周我一定要重新确立顺序，确保回到我平时的水平，因为整个周末我都开得像个老奶奶。所以这不是平时的基米。不过幸运的是，还有下一场比赛在等着我们，我非常期待。”
整个2026年，安东内利凭借摧枯拉朽般的速度和不懈的稳定性一次次展现了他的实力。而在巴库，他展示了成为冠军所需素质中同样重要的另一面。
detailEn: You win world championships on your bad days as much as you do on your good ones.

Kimi Antonelli's Azerbaijan Grand Prix weekend, which he rightly described as "the worst by far" of the season, was proof of that as he passed a test he would inevitably face at some point with flying colours. In doing so, he avoided a fate that befell Oscar Piastri in last year's unsuccessful pursuit of the Formula 1 title.

Minimising such performances is part of the title-winning equation, but it's essential to limit the damage when things go wrong. We knew Antonelli had the comfort of a gargantuan 81-point lead heading into the weekend, but what he demonstrated in Baku was he understands how to use it. That's something Piastri failed to do with the more slender, but still healthy, 31-point lead he took to Baku in 2025.

Piastri crashed in qualifying, moved before the start and knew a penalty was inevitable despite plummeting down the order, then crashed at Turn 5 on the first lap. The only saving grace was that McLaren team-mate and title rival Lando Norris didn't make the most of his opportunity, but even so this represented the start of Piastri's campaign unravelling.

I asked him during that year's Brazilian GP weekend about his struggles and it was Azerbaijan that he mentioned as a weekend when "you could argue there were some other things that maybe crept in" and compromised him. It's difficult to escape the conclusion that he was pointing to the hangover of the 'papaya rules' incident from Monza where he was ordered to let Norris past after his team-mate's slow pitstop.

Even without the complicating factor of such team-orders bafflement, Antonelli could so easily have let something similar happen, especially given he's still so inexperienced, after hitting the wall needlessly in Q1.

That was a significant error given there was no reason to take risks so early in qualifying. That blunder was perhaps the consequence of overreaching to close the pace deficit to Mercedes team-mate George Russell, perhaps because of his longstanding tendency to flirt a little too much with the extremities of the track this year, but while ideally he wouldn't have made the error he took exactly the right mentality into the race.

His recovery to fifth was aided by the safety car, but it was a steady, well-executed drive in which he deliberately left a margin and kept his head after sustaining floor damage through no fault of his own after contact with Ollie Bearman in the Turn 1 chaos of the first safety-car restart.
"I was driving a bit like my grandmother, just damage-safe mode, just didn't take a risk," said Antonelli. "Before making a move, I was making sure that I could go for it."

This showed wisdom that belies his inexperience that is often hard-won and at great cost by drivers who aren't such fast learners. He later elaborated on his reasons for this, as well as indicating that he quickly set aside any pretensions of a Monza-style recovery early in the grand prix. While he suggested he had "nothing to lose" after qualifying, when he spoke following the race he explained why that wasn't really the case.

"If I had the same pace as at Monza or in previous races, it would have been different," said Antonelli. "It would have been full attack. But I realised very early that, first of all, it was a lot harder to overtake with a train of cars all in overtake mode. And then I didn't have the same pace as I had previously. So the mindset changed very quickly.
"And also seeing so many people doing mistakes, you kind of pulled back a little bit. I just took advantage of everyone else's mistake and just moved forward."

Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff and others around him will have drummed that approach into him, but only Antonelli himself could lock into a mindset at odds with the attacking one that usually serves him so well. The result was losing 15 points to Russell in the championship rather than 25. A big hit, but not as big as it could have been.

Had he been too aggressive and crashed or collided with a rival and retired, the points loss would be multiplied by the mental scars he would carry into the run-in. Instead, Antonelli could finish a race he described as driving at 80% satisfied with his approach and able to lay down the gauntlet to Russell for the coming race in Malaysia.

"I'll make sure next week I re-establish the order and just make sure that I will be back at my usual level because this weekend I was driving more like a grandmother," he said. "So it wasn't the usual Kimi. But, luckily, we have another race coming up and I'm really looking forward to it."
Antonelli has showed his class time and again during 2026 with his pulverising pace and relentlessness. In Baku, he showed a different aspect that's just as important in the make-up of a champion.

detailZh: 夏尔·勒克莱尔：“迈凯伦和红牛迈出了我们没有迈出的那一步”
法拉利在阿塞拜疆大奖赛上过得艰难，因为对手F1车队为巴库带来了大量升级
勒克莱尔在F1阿塞拜疆大奖赛结束后认为，红牛如今在底盘性能方面对法拉利拥有明显优势，而迈凯伦也有了显著进步。
这两支车队都为巴库带来了重要的升级套件，重点集中在侧箱、底板和扩散器上——迈凯伦的升级还包括修改后的引擎盖、后悬架和尾翼，而红牛的升级则包含新的后视镜和座舱保护环（halo）。与此同时，法拉利的赛车则保持原样未做改动。
勒克莱尔在排位赛中惊险地锁定了头排发车位置，在第三节排位赛中以0.001秒的优势击败迈凯伦的奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里，并以0.137秒的优势击败红牛的伊萨克·哈贾尔。然而，这位摩纳哥车手到第四圈时已经远远落后于第五位；他最终能获得第四名，要归功于皮亚斯特里在一号弯刹车过晚冲出弯道的失误，以及基米·安东内利在排位赛中发生撞车、不得不从第16位发车在车阵中苦苦追赶。
“对我们来说，这场比赛有点无聊，”勒克莱尔说。“不幸的是，我们起步很糟糕，这可能是今天我们唯一能做得好得多的事情。在那之后，我们完全没有速度。和红牛相比，防守非常困难，因为我们的直道速度太慢了。”
“我们目前在原始速度上就是很挣扎。”
他补充道：“两辆红牛太快了，显然乔治·拉塞尔也相当强势。”
队友刘易斯·汉密尔顿对法拉利速度不足的问题则没有那么健谈。当被问到车队现在是否拥有第四快的赛车时，这位七届世界冠军回答道：“这有什么重要的？”
当Motorsport.com进一步追问红牛的速度有多么出人意料时——尽管马克斯·维斯塔潘在排位赛中落后1.6秒，却仍然挑战了乔治·拉塞尔的冠军，而伊萨克·哈贾尔在第三节排位赛中比梅赛德斯慢了一秒——汉密尔顿回应道：“我真的不会去想其他任何人。”
虽然勒克莱尔认为巴库赛道并不适合法拉利，但这位28岁的车手相信，SF-26这个周末表现不佳——尽管16号赛车再次使用了ADUO2动力单元——是因为对手们带来了升级。
“迈凯伦和红牛凭借他们带来的升级向前迈了一步，”他说。“他们最近进步了，向前迈出了我们没有做到的一步。而我们必须做出反应，因为现在损失一些速度之后要追回来会非常困难。所以希望我们能很快做出反应。”
研发显然受到预算上限和空气动力学测试限制的制约，但勒克莱尔表示，法拉利“即将有一些新东西带来”。
“至于这是否足以缩小差距，由于不知道其他车队还藏有什么底牌，那就是另一回事了，”他补充道，“但可以肯定的是，我们有一些新东西应该能帮助我们向前迈进一步。”
detailEn: Charles Leclerc: “McLaren and Red Bull did a step forward that we didn’t do”
Ferrari had a tough Azerbaijan GP, as rival F1 teams brought substantial upgrades to Baku
Red Bull now has a clear advantage over Ferrari in terms of chassis performance, with McLaren having also markedly improved, Charles Leclerc believes following the Formula 1 Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Both teams brought significant upgrade packages to Baku, focusing on the sidepods, floor and diffuser – McLaren’s also included a revised engine cover, rear suspension and rear wing while Red Bull’s featured new mirrors and halo. Meanwhile, Ferrari kept its car untouched.

Leclerc narrowly clinched a front-row spot on the grid, outpacing McLaren’s Oscar Piastri by 0.001s and Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar by 0.137s in Q3. However, the Monegasque faded to a distant fifth by lap four; he only finished fourth courtesy of a late mistake by Piastri, who ran deep into Turn 1, and Kimi Antonelli’s qualifying crash meaning he was fighting through the pack after starting 16th.

“It was a bit of a boring race for us,” Leclerc said. “Unfortunately, we had a bad start, which was probably the only thing we could have done much better today. After that, we just had no pace. Compared to the Red Bull, it was very difficult to defend because in the straight line we are too slow.
“We are just struggling with raw pace at the moment.”
He added: “The two Red Bulls were too quick and obviously George [Russell] was too strong as well.”

Team-mate Lewis Hamilton wasn’t as loquacious about Ferrari’s lack of speed. Asked if the Scuderia now had the fourth-fastest car, the seven-time world champion replied: “What’s the importance of that?”

Pressed by Motorsport.com on how unexpected Red Bull’s pace was – after Max Verstappen challenged George Russell for victory despite qualifying 1.6s down while Isack Hadjar was a second slower than the Mercedes in Q3 – Hamilton responded: “I don't really think about anybody else.”

While Leclerc doesn’t think the Baku track suits the Ferrari, the 28-year-old believes the SF-26’s lack of performance this weekend – despite running the ADUO2 power unit again on the #16 car – was down to the rivals' updates.

“McLaren and Red Bull did a step forward with the upgrades they are bringing,” he said. “They have grown recently, they did a step forward that we didn't do. And we must react, because losing some pace now is going to be very difficult to take it back. So hopefully we can react very soon.”
Development is obviously limited by the budget cap and the aerodynamic testing restrictions, but Ferrari has “a few things coming”, Leclerc indicated.

“Whether it's going to be enough to close the gap, not knowing what the others have in store as well is another matter,” he added. “But surely, we've got a few things that should help us do some steps forward.”
